rationale: This benchmark is a micro-program (333 text bytes, 4 functions) dominated by the deeply recursive Ackermann function, so control-flow obfuscation must be chosen carefully: FLA gets high SecurityGain/DiversityGain weights because flattening is the strongest structural disguise, but its RuntimeCost (0.9) and SizeCost (0.7) penalties are maximal because flattening a tiny recursive hot function multiplies both recursion dispatch overhead and relative text size dramatically, and CorrectnessRisk is elevated (0.4) since flattening recursive kernels can perturb loop-carried state; BCF is kept attractive (0.7 security) with moderate runtime penalty (0.6) since opaque predicates are cheap on a short call chain and add negligible absolute size to 48-208 byte functions; SUB and SPLIT get low cost/risk weights so they apply broadly — they are semantics-preserving, nearly free, and give good baseline diversity on such small functions; IBR and ICALL are favored moderately for their anti-analysis value (breaking static call/branch graph recovery, valuable in a program whose entire logic is one call graph) but tempered by runtime weight 0.5 due to indirect-dispatch overhead in the recursive hot path; IGV is weakest across the board because the program has essentially no global variable state to protect, so indirection there buys little security while still adding cost and risk.
